From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-show: lead files + ask on attribution methodology

Jonas / Ben,

I pulled an initial reconciliation between the raw CSV and our HubSpot import (see Drive link). High-level findings:

- ~1,120 rows in the raw export, 1,087 new/updated records created in HubSpot after import. The delta (~33) are mostly badge scans without an email; we created placeholder records.
- We’re seeing ~62 apparent duplicate emails across different companies (likely bounced or shared addresses).
- 18 records show a CRM Source of "Website" — those were overwritten by a marketing workflow that fires on contact creation; I’ll include the workflow id.

Suggested next steps (short playbook):
1) Run dedupe with primary key = email where present, else badge_id + company. Keep earliest touch as 'event_first_touch'.
2) Map placeholder/no-email records to a "manual review" bucket and do not auto-assign pipeline credit unless Ops confirms by review.
3) For dispute resolution: recommend 60% credit to event first-touch for early-stage pipeline (MQL > SQL within 90 days), and residual credit to last-touch for late-stage conversions.

I attached a preliminary attribution workbook (prelim-attrib-0609.xlsx) with a sample allocation calculation and the HubSpot workflow link. Ben — can you send the dedupe snapshot once run?

Marissa Cole
Senior Events Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: prelim-attrib-0609.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re: Fwd: Post-show: lead files + ask on attribution methodology

Quick update — ran the dedupe and export. Numbers:
- Raw scanner rows: 1,120
- HubSpot records created/updated: 1,087
- Exact-email duplicates found: 62
- Near-duplicate (typos/aliases): 17 (I applied a fuzzy match threshold of 0.85)

I pushed a dedupe snapshot to Drive (dedupe-snapshot-0610.json) and wrote a short note about matching rules. For the placeholder records (no-email), I extracted device ids and will hand those to ops for manual enrichment.

If Marissa wants to apply your 60/40 event-first-touch allocation, I can run that allocation in the workbook and produce a delta file showing which HubSpot deals would flip credit.

Ben Carter
Field Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachments: dedupe-snapshot-0610.json

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: MedInnovation — preliminary attribution & next steps

Hi Sarah,

Appreciate the patience — attached is our preliminary reconciliation and a short playbook (prelim-attrib-0609.xlsx) that shows the proposed allocation. TL;DR:
- We recommend assigning 60% first-touch credit to the event for deals that converted to SQL within 90 days; last-touch receives remaining 40%.
- 33 records without emails were set aside for manual review and not auto-attributed.
- After Ben’s dedupe pass we identified 79 duplicates/near-duplicates; allocation adjustments are included in the attached delta sheet.

We’ve noted the HubSpot workflow that overwrote source fields and will share recommended rule changes so event source persists on contact creation.

Next steps:
1) If MedInnovation agrees with the 60/40 play, we’ll produce a final report with line-item attribution and impacted deal ids by 15 Jun.
2) If you prefer a multi-touch model, we can run a separate run and compare uplift.

Attachments: prelim-attrib-0609.xlsx

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Field Partnerships
Redwood Inference
